stem:
Kavya writes a two-digit number as $10a+b$ and the number with its digits reversed as $10b+a$, with digits $a \neq b$.

Which two claims correctly justify a divisibility fact with place value?

options.text: $(10a+b)-(10b+a)=9(a-b)$, so the difference of the number and its reverse is a multiple of $9$.
Read $a$ and $b$ as separate digit marks only, with no place-value expression for either number.
Because the difference factors as $9(a-b)$, both $10a+b$ and $10b+a$ leave the same remainder on division by $9$.
Choose the largest product among placements of $a$ and $b$, and treat that product rule as this reverse-digit test.

teacher.key_rationale: Place-value forms give difference 9(a-b), hence same remainder mod 9. Digits as marks only omit place value. Largest-product placement is a different mechanism.
